channel.title: MagSolutionsAI Blog
channel.description: Analysis of AI-generated code supply chain risk: slopsquatting, hallucinated dependencies, and how to verify what your assistant just suggested.

item.title: Thirteen npm packages, 48 seconds, one fake wallet SDK
item.description: On 7 September 2026, GitHub's Advisory Database flagged 13 npm packages named after Coinbase's wallet infrastructure as malware. Registry timestamps show all 13 were published within 48 seconds of each other.

item.title: The malicious package that never showed up in anyone's requirements.txt
item.description: Two PyPI packages published this week show why checking your direct dependencies is not enough. The credential-stealing code was one dependency away, in a package nobody typed into a requirements file on purpose.

item.title: What is slopsquatting, and why your scanner cannot see it
item.description: Attackers no longer wait for you to mistype a package name. They register the names your AI assistant invents. Here is how the attack works and why CVE-based tooling is blind to it by design.

item.title: The package that never existed and got 30,000 downloads
item.description: In 2024 a researcher registered huggingface-cli, a name AI models kept recommending but which was never real. Three months later it had over 30,000 downloads — including from a major tech company's public documentation.

item.title: How to check whether a package actually exists before you install it
item.description: A practical guide to verifying Python and npm dependencies against the live registries — the exact commands, what the responses mean, and the check most people forget after the first one passes.
